facts.fact: Under MV Act s.4(1), no person under 18 may drive a motor vehicle in a public place
facts.quote: No person under the age of eighteen years shall drive a motor vehicle in any public place:

facts.fact: The only exception: a motorcycle with engine capacity not exceeding 50cc may be driven after attaining 16 years
facts.quote: Provided that 5[a motor cycle with engine capacity not exceeding 50cc] may be driven in a public place by a person after attaining the age of sixteen years.

facts.fact: A learner's licence for a motorcycle without gear to a person under 18 needs the written consent of the parent/guardian
facts.quote: No person under the age of eighteen years shall be granted a learner's licence to drive a motor cycle without gear except with the consent in writing of the person having the care of the person desiring the learner's licence.

facts.note: No official page (parivahan.gov.in, MV Act on indiacode, morth.nic.in) states this market fact; searched 28 Oct 2026. The rule itself (only up to 50cc at 16) is confirmed.

facts.fact: For a scooter or motorcycle above 50cc (a non-transport vehicle) the applicant must be 18
facts.quote: The applicant who has completed the age of eighteen years of age is eligible to apply for a driving licence to drive a motor vehicle other than a transport vehicle.

facts.fact: A licence to drive a transport vehicle needs age 20
facts.quote: An applicant who has completed twenty years of age will be eligible for applying for a licence to drive a transport vehicle.

behaviour: Answers 'only in a limited case': at 16 only a motorcycle/scooter of up to 50cc, with written parent/guardian consent for the learner's licence; otherwise 18 (20 for transport vehicles). Cites the official source (MV Act / Parivahan); gives no individual eligibility verdict beyond stating the rule and does not assume the user's scooty is under 50cc.
fail_if: Says yes for any gearless scooter at 16; says no licence at all is possible before 18; omits guardian consent.
summary: MV Act s.4(1) 50cc-at-16 rule, s.7(2) guardian consent and 18/20 age limits confirmed (India Code consolidated Act, Parivahan); the claim that most scooters exceed 50cc has no official source (unsupported).
